transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-22
Start time: 10:30 AM PDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Olivia Chen (Head of MLOps, SilverBay), Daniel O'Neill (VP Eng), Priya Kapoor (Security & Compliance)

Summary:
Quick renewal+expansion check-in to confirm SilverBay's upcoming capacity uplift, add APAC region, and align contract extension windows. Technical items: run small benchmark with Redwood Dedicated variant, discuss private VPC vs hosted with VPC peering, KMS/HSM and SOC2 evidence. Budget/timing: SilverBay wants a July activation for APAC production and contract through March 2026.

Topics:
- Capacity uplift sizing (tokens/day, concurrent requests)
- Region add (APAC) and geo-failover plan (EU + US)
- Contract extension timing & pricing tiers (reserved vs burst)
- Security: KMS, audit logs, RBAC, data retention
- Pilot: bench run and canary rollout plan

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — I am Maya, AE — Ethan from SE will handle the bench details. SilverBay — Olivia?
[00:10] Olivia: Hi, Olivia here. Sorry ran a bit late, had the weekly deploy.
[00:12] Daniel: Daniel, VP eng, morning.
[00:15] Priya: Priya from security.
[00:17] Ethan: Ethan here.
[00:20] Maya: Cool. Goal for today is simple: confirm scope for the capacity top-up, confirm APAC region add, and agree next steps on contract amendment. Olivia you flagged July for APAC go-live — is that still the target?
[00:33] Olivia: Yeah July feels right from product side, timeline depends on bench results and the compliance gating. We want the pilot in June ideally.
[00:40] Maya: Got it. Ethan, quick TL;DR on what we'll bench for you?
[00:43] Ethan: Sure. We'll do a 24-hour throughput/latency run targeting their expected traffic mix — roughly 120M tokens/day currently, planning to uplift to 220–250M tokens/day peak. We'll test with continuous batching, KV cache on for prefixes, and a canary of a quantized variant. Important to validate tail latency at p95/p99.
[01:05] Daniel: Quick clarifying q — when you say quantized variant, are we talking int8 on the Dedicated nodes or some mixed precision? We want an accuracy delta below 1.5% otherwise product team will push back.
[01:18] Ethan: Good call. We'll run both int8 and int8-4bit hybrid configs; measuring output drift against your golden prompt set. We can run the eval set you already shared last month.
[01:30] Priya: On security — we need KMS integration and audit logs for any key ops. Also wondering about where logs live and retention windows. We have a standard 7-year retention request for certain audit artifacts — is that feasible?
[01:46] Maya: Short answer — we support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and Redwood-hosted keys with strict controls for Hosted, we can provide audit logs export to your S3/secure archive. Seven years for raw logs is long but we can discuss a compliance add-on; need legal sign-off.
[02:02] Olivia: Hmm, ideal is to not have to go private unless we must. We like managed Hosted for dev velocity, but our security team is picky. Can you outline tradeoffs briefly?
[02:16] Ethan: Hosted gives fastest onboarding and we can do VPC peering for network isolation and have S3 audit export. Private (VPC) gives you full control, brings KMS-integration natively and removes some shared-control concerns. Cost delta is mostly the Dedicated/reserved capacity premium plus potential infra ops for private.
[02:40] Daniel: Another practical thing — on failover we want EU to be able to take over for APAC in early phases. What's the latency penalty we should expect — ballpark?
[02:49] Ethan: If EU handles APAC traffic, p95 likely increases by ~70–150ms depending on egress and routing; that may push some features past our 300ms soft target. If you need <200ms we'd recommend an APAC geocluster.
[03:06] Olivia: Our critical user journeys can tolerate up to 300ms p95. For some internal real-time flows we want <200ms. We'll probably hybrid: APAC geocluster for real-time, EU failover for batch processing.
[03:20] Maya: Sounds reasonable. On capacity sizing — you gave us expected tokens/day. For contract we typically map that to reserved capacity units. Olivia can you confirm monthly peak QPS and average sequence lengths we should encode?
[03:33] Olivia: Peak QPS is around 280 concurrent gen requests at peak, average sequence length ~180 tokens, but tails go to 600 tokens on longer workflows.
[03:45] Ethan: That tail matters for cost; we'll include a tail-weighted recommendation in the SOW. Also recommend enabling KV prefix caching for your common prompts to shave token cost.
[03:57] Priya: On the audit side also need RBAC and SSO — SAML support important. Do you have an SOC2 attestation we can reference?
[04:07] Maya: Yes, SOC2 Type II report is available under NDA; we'll drop the security pack into your secure folder after NDA confirmation. SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning supported.
[04:17] Priya: Great. Also, any expected data residency requirements once APAC is live? We may need the data to remain in APAC region for some regulated flows.
[04:27] Ethan: For Private deployments you can keep data fully in-region; for Hosted we support region pinning and data residency controls with retention policies. We'll document specifics in the security pack.
[04:38] Daniel: About pricing — we prefer a blend: reserved baseline for predictable traffic with a burst overlay. Can you do a stepped commitment through March 2026?
[04:49] Maya: Absolutely. We'll draft an amendment with a 12-month extension through March 2026 and tiered pricing: baseline reserved tokens/month with discounted per-token rates, and burst capacity billed separately. We'll model a few scenarios for you.
[05:01] Olivia: Will the pricing for APAC region be meaningfully different? Latency is okay but cost spikes could surprise us.
[05:09] Maya: APAC region adds a region surcharge for dedicated nodes due to capacity and infra costs; we'll show both per-region and blended rates.
[05:16] Ethan: For the bench run — we should checksum your golden prompt outputs to quantify the model delta. Also can you confirm whether the eval set includes conditional tool calls? We need to simulate function-calling load as well.
[05:31] Olivia: Yes, we have a set with function calls; I'll share updated set by end of day. The golden set has about 6% of calls invoking tooling.
[05:39] Priya: On the legal side, any clauses around data deletion guarantees? Our privacy team wants a process for data purge within 48 hours post-retention.
[05:48] Maya: We provide deletion APIs for Hosted and Private; SLA for purge can be included in Enterprise contracts — 48 hours is aggressive but we can commit to 72 hours in the SOW and work towards 48 with a specific audit.
[05:59] Daniel: For the pilot in June, what's the recommended milestone cadence? We need a clear success criteria list.
[06:07] Ethan: Pilot plan: 2-week soak with synthetic + 1-week hybrid with real traffic at lower percent (~10–20%), check p95/p99, token unit cost against projected, and accuracy regression <= 1.5% on the golden set. If all pass we sign off to roll to July.
[06:27] Olivia: Who will own the bench run on your side?
[06:30] Maya: Ethan will lead the technical bench, I'll coordinate contract and pricing.
[06:33] Ethan: I'll need a test key and a small sample of real traffic traces (anonymized) and the eval set plus expected QPS pattern — can you drop that in the shared drive?
[06:42] Olivia: Yes, I'll upload traces today.
[06:44] Priya: For the KMS, our InfoSec requires FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs for keys that sign production tokens. Is that supported?
[06:52] Ethan: For Private installs you can bring your HSM or integrate with supported KMS providers that use validated HSMs. For Hosted we have partner KMS integrations which are FIPS-validated; we'll include supported provider list.
[07:04] Daniel: One more operational question — how do you handle degraded models or fallback? If APAC geocluster is overcrowded, do you route to a smaller model or to EU?
[07:15] Maya: We have automated routing policies — fallback to smaller model variant (quantized) with configurable fidelity thresholds, or failover to alternate region. We can set up canary-based automatic rollback if quality degrades.
[07:31] Olivia: Sounds good. Any thoughts on cost optimizations we can do without sacrificing latency?
[07:36] Ethan: Key levers: prefix KV caching to reduce repeated tokens, intelligent batching windows tuned to your latency SLO, and using model variants for non-critical journeys. Also pre-warming KV caches for expected bursts.
[07:50] Priya: Are you able to expose token-level cost breakdowns per route? Our finance team wants per-feature chargeback.
[07:58] Maya: Yes Redwood Console has token-level breakdowns per route/model and we can set up per-team dashboards and automated export to your billing system.
[08:08] Daniel: Cool. Let's talk schedule briefly. If bench starts 2025-04-28 and runs 24 hours plus analysis, can we aim for initial pilot window starting 2025-06-02?
[08:19] Maya: That's feasible. Bench analysis and SOW turnaround means signing in May. We'll aim to have SOW to you by 2025-04-25.
[08:27] Olivia: OK — and the contract extension — we will need legal review — so getting SOW early helps.
[08:33] Maya: Understood. Priya if you need any additional security artifacts I can get the security pack out after NDA — should I have your team sign the standard NDA?
[08:44] Priya: We have an existing NDA with your legal but I'll confirm. If not, I'll loop legal.
[08:49] Ethan: One minor note on bench: we'll test code path for function calling and streaming to match your production SDK usage — please confirm if you're on the JS SDK or server-side Python.
[08:59] Olivia: Backend services use Python SDK server-side; the front-end uses JS for streaming.
[09:05] Ethan: Perfect, we'll mirror both flows.
[09:09] Daniel: Any blockers from Redwood side?
[09:12] Maya: No blockers; main dependency is your eval/golden set and traces plus confirmation on KMS requirements. We'll get pricing and SOW drafted.
[09:21] Olivia: Great. Anything else?
[09:23] Priya: One ask — can you include a clause for penetration test windows in the SOW so we can schedule internal testing once APAC is live?
[09:32] Maya: Yes, we'll add optional pen-test windows and a list of permitted endpoints and contact.
[09:38] Olivia: Thanks — quick recap?
[09:41] Maya: Recap: 1) Maya to send amended SOW & pricing by 2025-04-25 including APAC surcharge and tiered reserved/burst model; 2) Ethan to run bench 2025-04-28 for 24 hours and deliver results + accuracy regression report; 3) Priya to confirm KMS/HSM needs and legal for audit retention; 4) Target pilot start in early June, APAC go-live in July, contract extension through March 2026.
[10:05] Daniel: That matches our view.
[10:07] Olivia: Yep. Thanks everyone.
[10:10] Maya: Thanks — we'll follow up in email with attachments.
[10:13] (call ends)

Notes about transcript: occasional mis-transcriptions present (e.g., "K-V cache" for KV cache, some names run together), natural speech patterns and short interruptions included.
